entry.title: Stats on compact block reconstructions
entry.summary:
The analysis of block propagation delays within the Bitcoin network, as illustrated by graphs from KIT, reveals nuanced insights into blockchain dynamics. Over the past year, the data indicates a consistent decline in the delay times at the 90% percentile, while delays at the 50% percentile have remained unchanged. This trend suggests that while the majority of the network experiences faster block confirmations, median times have not improved.
Interestingly, the correlation between block propagation and compact block reconstruction rates raises questions about network efficiency, especially in the context of latency. The latency history chart shows deteriorated latency figures around the time when compact block relay began necessitating round trips. Given typical ping times of 30ms-40ms, as per the latency chart, each round-trip during the reconstruction process adds approximately 40ms per hop. Additionally, the initial block validation by the announcer could add a significant delay ranging from 50ms to 300ms. This cumulative latency could affect overall network performance, although it appears that it might be mitigated somewhat by the network's topology, where a well-connected node can reach 50% of the network within roughly two hops.
Several factors could potentially explain the observed decrease in the 90% block propagation delays. These include improvements in validation times, upgrades in node hardware, and possibly more frequent use of cached unspent transaction outputs (UTXOs). Another perspective considers the possibility of increased network centralization; a higher concentration of sybil nodes implies faster propagation since reaching one such node effectively means reaching many. However, the specific influence of such factors remains speculative without more detailed data.
Moreover, the decrease in propagation delays coincides with the relaunch of the FIBRE network, as announced in February 2026. While one might expect this enhancement to result in abrupt improvements (a step function change), the steady decrease observed could suggest a gradual integration or optimization within the network post-relaunch. For further clarity and insights into these phenomena, continuous monitoring and analysis of network data are essential, as provided by resources like [KIT](https://www.dsn.kastel.kit.edu/bitcoin/) and updates on developments like the [localhost's FIBRE network relaunch](https://lclhost.org/blog/fibre-resurrected/).
